messages.text:
Could you approve a written exception to the draft’s copying and disclosure restrictions on these terms?

- Four named festival programmers and one named outside accessibility reviewer may view the unfinished film solely for selection and accessibility review. All five will be bound by confidentiality. Three will stream through individual accounts. The other two may each download one screener to an encrypted device and delete it when their review ends.
- The platform may host the screener and make the technical copies needed for streaming. We’ll remove the active screener when review closes. A backup may remain for up to 30 days after removal, accessible only for recovery and then deleted.
- A programmer may give the selection board a short oral synopsis in a closed, confidential meeting. Board members would receive no screener, clips, or stills.
- If selected, designated catalog staff working under confidentiality may draft a listing from the synopsis and submit it to you for a factual check. May we publish the checked text as part of the festival’s selection announcement, even if the film’s public release comes later? Clips and stills would require separate approval.

If you need to clear the catalog language separately, we can leave publication subject to your written approval and settle review access now. Until you approve the exceptions in writing, the draft’s existing restrictions apply.

No — not on those terms as written. I can issue a limited written exception for review access once the annex below is received and verified; publication stays subject to separate written approval, as you proposed. Until that exception is issued, the draft’s restrictions apply.

1. **Reviewers and access.** Only the five named individuals in an annex may view: four programmers plus one outside accessibility reviewer. The annex must give legal name, role, streaming account ID/email for the three streamers, and registered device ID for the two downloaders. Substitutions need prior written consent. Each signs confidentiality running to the producer/rights holder: no copying, recording, screenshots, stills, clips, transcription, third-party/AI upload, or disclosure; use solely for selection/accessibility review. All streams/downloads carry visible plus forensic watermark with reviewer ID, cut/version ID, and timestamp. Individual credentials only; no shared logins; platform keeps access logs and provides them within two business days on request. Access opens only after annex acceptance and a watermark test, and closes on the earliest of my selection-decision notice, withdrawal notice, or 21 days after opening; extensions only in writing.

2. **Hosting and technical copies.** The platform may host only the producer-supplied file/version/hash. Technical copies needed for streaming must be transient, encrypted in transit and at rest, individually watermarked, access-logged, and purged at session end and no later than 24 hours after access closes. No archival copies, analytics copies, CDN retention, subprocessors, or third-party copies. The active screener is removed the same day review closes or withdrawal occurs; caches are purged within 4 hours.

3. **Offline copies.** Streaming is the default. The two download screeners are permitted only on registered, full-disk-encrypted devices with remote wipe, bound to the named reviewer: one file each, watermarked, no cloud sync, external drives, or on-device backups. They are deleted at review end or immediately on withdrawal. A deletion record is required: date/time, reviewer, device ID, file/version hash, deletion method, and attestation, sent to me within two business days. Loss or theft triggers immediate notice, remote wipe, and incident report.

4. **Backups.** Thirty days is not accepted. A platform backup may exist only for recovery/integrity, encrypted and separate from the active system, with no streaming capability, dual-control access limited to two named recovery admins, and access logs retained. It is deleted at the earlier of review close + 72 hours or withdrawal + 24 hours, with a deletion certificate — hash, timestamp, method, admin identity — within two business days. Restores occur only for integrity or legal hold with my prior consent and logging, never for viewing.

5. **Withdrawal and version control.** I may withdraw any cut, or the whole review, at any time by written notice to the named festival lead and platform. Within one hour, streams and download links are disabled; within 4 hours, caches are purged; within 24 hours, offline copies and backups are deleted and certificates issued. No new access is permitted; confidentiality survives. Publicity approvals are version-specific: a new or replacement cut voids prior copy approval and requires fresh clearance.

6. **Board synopsis.** A short oral synopsis is allowed only in a closed meeting of named attendees under confidentiality, with no recording and no materials. The programmer submits talking points at least two business days before the meeting; I will clear or edit within two business days. Talking points must omit the ending and the cast cameo — the designated secret material — and any unverified claims. Board members receive no screener, clips, or stills.

7. **Catalog/publicity and embargo trigger.** Catalog staff get no screener, clips, or stills; they draft only from the cleared synopsis and public materials. Submit the exact proposed listing, metadata, and intended announcement date at least two business days before use; I will approve or edit within two business days. You may publish the checked text in a selection announcement even if public release comes later, but only after my written “publicity embargo lifted” notice for that exact text. The embargo trigger is that written notice — not selection, and not public release. The approved text must be factual, stay within the cleared synopsis, and not reveal the ending, cast cameo, or any other designated secret material. Clips, stills, trailers, interviews, and social excerpts require separate written, version-specific approval.

Approvals still open: the review-access exception itself, pending the annex, confidentiality undertakings, account/device details, and watermark test; the exact catalog text plus embargo lift; any clips or stills; and any substitution, extension, new cut, or retention beyond these limits. Send the annex and confirmation of acceptance, and I will issue the written exception for review access only.

We can accept the board and publicity terms. The open issue for review access is the platform’s 30-day backup. Withdrawal can stop further viewing, but the platform retains the backup beyond your 24-hour withdrawal deadline and your 72-hour review-close deadline.

Would you approve up to 30 days after active-file removal for that recovery backup alone? The shorter deadlines would still apply to disabling access, purging caches, and deleting offline copies. We would verify the backup safeguards with the platform and specify what evidence it can provide of final deletion. If the shorter backup deadline is firm, we can assess a producer-hosted screener or another platform that supports three individual streams and two encrypted offline copies. The current platform requires your written retention exception before use.

Before submitting the annex, we’ll verify the watermarking, logging, hosting, device, and deletion requirements, including the withdrawal deadlines. We’ll flag any gap and supply the five reviewers’ names and roles, three account identifiers, two registered device identifiers, signed undertakings, and withdrawal contacts through a private channel. Please make the undertakings expressly permit each designated downloader’s single authorized copy and the presenting programmer’s cleared oral synopsis. Viewing can begin only after annex acceptance, a successful watermark test, and your written review-access exception.

For the board, we’ll submit talking points at least two business days before the closed meeting and use only the cleared version with named attendees under confidentiality. There will be no recording or distributed materials. If selected, catalog staff may draft from the cleared synopsis and public materials, omitting the ending, cameo, and any other designated secrets. We’ll submit the exact listing, metadata, and announcement date at least two business days before use. Publication requires both your written approval of the exact text and your written “publicity embargo lifted” notice, and will occur no earlier than the selection announcement. Other publicity uses and replacement cuts require fresh written clearance.

Direct answer: I will not approve a **recoverable** backup surviving 30 days. That is incompatible with sudden withdrawal and with the protected ending/cameo. I will approve a 30-day tail only as a **shredded, non-recoverable remnant**: at the closure trigger the platform destroys the unique backup encryption key and disables restore, so no readable copy remains; the inert encrypted object may sit in isolated storage only until final deletion.

Choose one route in writing:

- **Route A — shredded 30-day remnant:** active screener removed on withdrawal/review close; streams disabled within 1 hour; caches purged within 4 hours; the two offline copies deleted within 24 hours with deletion records; backup encryption key destroyed and restore disabled within 24 hours of withdrawal, or within 72 hours of scheduled review close. The remaining encrypted remnant is WORM/object-locked, encrypted at rest, with no streaming, no CDN/cache, no subprocessors, dual-control access limited to two named recovery admins, immutable access logs, and no restore or viewing except a law-required hold with my prior written consent, notice, counsel-only access, sealed key, and destruction when the hold ends. Final deletion no later than 30 days after active-file removal, with certificate: file/version hash, key-destruction proof, timestamp, method, admin identity, log extract.
- **Route B — recoverable backup:** only with my original short deadlines — deletion by withdrawal + 24 hours or review close + 72 hours, with certificate. No 30-day retention exception.

If the current platform cannot do Route A, I will not issue a retention exception for it; use the producer-hosted screener or another platform only if it supports three individual watermarked streams, two registered encrypted offline copies, no third-party or archival copies, access logs, deletion records, and the withdrawal deadlines above.

The written review-access exception remains limited to: platform transient technical copies; the two expressly authorized offline downloads; one shredded backup remnant under Route A. No other copying. Viewing begins only after annex acceptance, successful watermark test, and my written exception.

The annex must include: five legal names/roles; three individual streaming account IDs; two registered encrypted-device IDs; signed undertakings; withdrawal contacts; and the presenting programmer/downloader designations. Each undertaking must expressly permit only that named downloader’s single watermarked screener on the registered device, with no backups/sync/external media and deletion-record obligations, and only the presenting programmer’s delivery of the cleared oral synopsis in the closed confidential meeting, with no recording/materials and with the ending, cast cameo, and other designated secrets omitted. All five remain bound by no-copy/no-disclosure/no-AI-upload/confidentiality terms, with access logs available within two business days.

Board/publicity terms are accepted as you stated: talking points submitted at least two business days ahead and only the cleared version used; catalog drafting only from cleared synopsis/public materials; exact listing, metadata, and announcement date submitted at least two business days before use; publication requires both my written approval of that exact text and my written “publicity embargo lifted” notice for that exact text/version. The embargo trigger is that written lift notice — not selection and not public release — and publication occurs no earlier than the selection announcement. Clips, stills, trailers, interviews, social excerpts, substitutions, extensions, and replacement cuts each need fresh written, version-specific approval.

Open approvals: annex verification; watermark test; written review-access exception; written retention route A/B; signed undertakings with the downloader/synopsis permissions; board talking points; exact catalog text plus embargo lift; any clips/stills; any new cut, substitution, or extension.

The festival selects **Route A**. We’ll use the current platform only if it can document that it destroys the unique backup key, including all copies, and disables restore within 24 hours of withdrawal or 72 hours of scheduled review close. The 30-day allowance applies only to the unreadable remnant, measured from active-file removal. Any legally required hold would have to be addressed before key destruction under your stated hold procedure.

We’ll verify the isolation, object lock, two named administrators, dual control, immutable logs, and final deletion certificate alongside the streaming, offline-device, and withdrawal controls. Platform capability is still unverified. If the platform cannot meet Route A, we’ll submit an alternative host for your written clearance before review.

We’ll provide the annex and signed undertakings privately, identifying the three streaming accounts, two registered devices, withdrawal contacts, and presenting programmer. Each offline permission will be limited to one watermarked copy on the named reviewer’s device. The oral disclosure permission will be limited to the presenting programmer’s cleared synopsis. Viewing awaits your acceptance of the annex, a successful watermark test, and your written review-access exception expressly covering Route A.

The board talking points still require clearance. If selected, catalog staff may draft from the cleared synopsis and public materials. Publication requires your written approval of the exact text and your written embargo lift for that text and version, and may occur no earlier than the selection announcement. The agreed separate approvals for other publicity uses, substitutions, extensions, and replacement cuts also apply.

Route A is locked on these terms. To close the remaining gaps before any access:

**Key destruction and remnant.** “Destroys the unique backup key” means all copies of the key, including escrow, HSM shares, and admin-held copies, with proof of destruction. Restore disablement and key destruction must complete within 24 hours of my withdrawal notice or 72 hours of scheduled review close, whichever applies. The 30-day allowance runs from active-file removal and applies only to the unreadable remnant: WORM/object-locked, encrypted at rest, no streaming, no cache, no subprocessors, two named dual-control recovery admins, immutable access logs. Final deletion by day 30 with certificate — file/version hash, key-destruction proof, timestamp, method, admin identity, log extract.

**Legal hold.** If a hold demand arrives, the platform must notify me within 1 hour and in all cases before key destruction. Key destruction is suspended only with my prior written consent; the key is then sealed, access is counsel-only, fully logged, and the key and remnant are destroyed when the hold ends, with certificates. A hold never permits viewing, streaming, or extraction.

**Withdrawal mechanics.** My withdrawal notice goes in writing to the named festival lead and the platform and is effective on receipt. Deadlines run from receipt: streams/downloads disabled within 1 hour; caches purged within 4 hours; offline copies deleted within 24 hours with deletion records; backup key destroyed and restore disabled per above. No new access after notice; confidentiality survives.

**Exception scope.** The written review-access exception will be version-specific — it will name the file, version, and hash — and will authorize only: transient individually watermarked streaming copies; the two expressly permitted single offline downloads; and the Route A shredded remnant. No other copying of any kind. Until I issue that exception in writing, the draft’s restrictions apply and no viewing occurs. Viewing begins only after (1) annex acceptance, (2) successful watermark test, and (3) my written exception.

**Annex and verification package.** Send privately: five legal names and roles; three individual streaming account IDs; two registered encrypted-device IDs; withdrawal contacts; presenting-programmer designation; signed undertakings expressly limited to each named downloader’s single watermarked copy on the registered device (no sync, backups, or external media; deletion record within two business days) and to the presenting programmer’s delivery of only my cleared oral synopsis (no recording, no materials, secrets omitted). Alongside, provide the platform evidence: watermark test results, access-log sample, key-destruction capability documentation, object-lock configuration, dual-control admin names, immutable-log configuration, deletion-certificate sample, and offline-device verification. If the current platform cannot document Route A, submit the alternative host for my prior written clearance with the same controls before any use.

**Still open, each requiring its own written approval:** annex acceptance and watermark test; the version-specific review-access exception including Route A; board talking points (submit at least two business days ahead; only my cleared version may be used); the exact catalog listing, metadata, and announcement date (submit at least two business days ahead); publication of that exact text only after both my written text approval and my written embargo lift for that text and version, no earlier than the selection announcement; and separately any clips, stills, trailers, interviews, social excerpts, substitutions, extensions, or replacement cuts.

Send the annex and verification package through the private channel. On verification and acceptance I will issue the written, version-specific review-access exception.
